reaction: The different jobs of the clear parts and the iris make sense.

expectation: I expect the light-sensitive cells to connect to nerve cells, forming part of a pathway for signals from the eye.

effect: The light-sensitive lining is called the retina, and its outgoing bundle is the optic nerve. Both initial goals are complete.
reaction: The picture makes the new names easier to connect to their jobs.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and joining the focusing front to the retina should bring the eye parts together.
expectation: I expect a more complete eye that focuses light onto the retina, though it may still need to connect to the body and leaf.

effect: The focusing front and retina now form an eye with a nerve leaving its back.
reaction: The cutaway makes the parts' positions clear.
reason: The only offered combination connects the eye to the repaired body, as the goal requires.

effect: The eyes are now connected by nerves toward the brain; the leaf remains to be seen.
reaction: The nerve route is clear, though the result doesn't yet show how the leaf becomes a sight.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should complete the goal of seeing the leaf.
expectation: I expect light reflected from the leaf to enter the eyes and lead to signals reaching the brain.

effect: The completed picture connects reflected light reaching the retina with nerve signals travelling toward the brain, completing the sight goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the whole route from leaf to brain, though the picture only briefly explains how the brain makes sense of it.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the retina and optic nerve was worthwhile: the picture and explanation gave names and jobs to the light-sensitive lining and its outgoing fibres.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the completed eye to the body was clear but felt mostly like an assembly step; it didn't yet show how sight worked.

surprise.text: I learned that the retina is the light-sensitive lining and that its fibres gather into the optic nerve.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless. After the first choice, though, the combinations were the only offered actions, so there was little opportunity for another meaningful decision.

continue.text: I might continue to see another body system connected, but the mostly one-option assembly sequence makes me only mildly curious.
